ABSENCE: no test asserts that a failed tombstone leaves the entry pending (the documented fallback contract)
advisory.finding: No test asserts the distinct operator-facing warning that the permanent-rejection branch is specifically introduced to emit. The change's stated contract is that a CHANGE_INPUT failure is 'logged with a distinct warning naming the ticket, the class, and the shared RESOLUTION_MESSAGES remedy, so an operator sees a wedge instead of silence' (and worded so it cannot be confused with the transient 'will retry after lease' line). Both new tests assert only queue state and call count; a regression that emitted the transient line, dropped the ResolutionClass/message_for remedy text, or otherwise garbled the operator signal would still tombstone the entry and pass every assertion.
merged_from: The best-effort tombstone-failure fallback in _record_item_failure is untested. When _queue.mark_done raises, the code swallows it, logs 'could not tombstone %s; it stays pending', and (per its own contract) restores the old looping behavior for that entry. No test injects a mark_done failure, so neither the observable outcome (entry stays pending / re-pickable) nor the distinct fallback log is exercised for the permanent path.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_permanent_input_rejection_reaches_a_terminal_state, wrap the drain in `with caplog.at_level("WARNING", logger="rebar.llm.enrich_drain")` and assert `any("permanently rejected" in r.getMessage() and "will NOT retry" in r.getMessage() and tid in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)` and that the message_for(ResolutionClass.CHANGE_INPUT.value) text appears.
